question: You are responsible for managing the recommendation engine on an ecommerce website. The current model is deployed on a public Agent Platform endpoint and is actively serving production traffic. You have developed an updated version of the model and registered the model in Model Registry. You need to perform an A/B test to compare the new model’s performance to the current model. You plan to implement a traffic split, routing 10% of all incoming production requests to the new model and sending the remaining 90% to the current model. You want this transition to be transparent, and require no modifications to the client application that calls the endpoint. What should you do?

options.A: Deploy the new model to a serverless Cloud Run service. Implement logic in the client application that routes 10% of user requests to the Cloud Run service and the rest to the original endpoint.
options.B: Deploy the new model to the Agent Platform endpoint where the current model is deployed. Configure the endpoint’s traffic split to allocate 10% of user requests to the new model.
options.C: Create two separate Agent Platform Pipelines, one for each model version. Use Agent Platform Experiments to run both pipelines simultaneously. Configure the experiment to send 10% of user requests to the new model’s pipeline and the rest to the production model’s pipeline.
options.D: Deploy the new model to a new Agent Platform endpoint. Configure Cloud Load Balancing to send 10% of user requests to the new endpoint and the rest to the original endpoint.

discussion: Selected Answer: B Correct answer: B. Deploying both model versions to the same Agent Platform endpoint and configuring a 10/90 traffic split provides transparent A/B testing without requiring any client application changes; A and D require additional routing infrastructure or client changes, while C misuses Pipelines and Experiments, which are not designed for routing live production traffic. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Option B is correct because Vertex AI (formerly AI/Agent Platform) Endpoints natively support deploying multiple models to a single endpoint and configuring a traffic split between them. This allows you to split traffic (e.g., 90/10) dynamically without making any changes to the client application. Options A and D require either client-side modifications or additional unnecessary infrastructure, while Option C incorrectly attempts to use pipelines for real-time traffic splitting.

question: You are developing an AI text generator that will be able to dynamically adapt its generated responses to mirror the writing style of the user and mimic famous authors if their style is detected. You have a large dataset of various authors’ works, and you plan to host the model on a custom VM. You want to use the most effective model. What should you do?

options.A: Fine-tune the latest Llama model from Model Garden on Agent Platform Serverless Training.
options.B: Use the latest Gemini Flash foundational model.
options.C: Deploy the latest Llama model from Model Garden, and use prompt engineering.
options.D: Fine-tune a BERT-based model from Hugging Face.

discussion: [VERIFIED STUDY NOTE] OPTION A IS CORRECT (counters AI Answer C). Fine-tune the latest Llama model from Model Garden on Agent Platform Serverless Training. Prompt engineering (Option C) is inefficient for a large corpus of author styles, BERT (Option D) cannot generate text, and Gemini Flash (Option B) cannot be self-hosted on a custom VM.

Selected Answer: A Correct answer: A. Fine-tuning a generative Llama model on a dataset of authors’ works is the most effective way to teach the model specific writing styles, while Agent Platform Serverless Training provides managed scalable training; B is a general foundation model without style-specific tuning, C relies only on prompts and is less effective for consistently learning many styles, and D uses BERT, which is primarily designed for language understanding rather than text generation. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: OPTION A IS CORRECT (counters AI Answer C). Fine-tune the latest Llama model from Model Garden on Agent Platform Serverless Training. Prompt engineering (Option C) is inefficient for a large corpus of author styles, BERT (Option D) cannot generate text, and Gemini Flash (Option B) cannot be self-hosted on a custom VM. — When a project requires self-hosting a model on custom VM infrastructure and deeply adapting its generation to mimic diverse author styles from a large custom corpus, fine-tuning an open-weights foundation model (such as Llama 3) is the optimal strategy. Vertex AI Serverless Custom Training allows scalable fine-tuning without managing training servers, and the resulting customized model weights can be exported and deployed to any target VM environment.

question: You are the lead ML engineer for a large ecommerce company. The Data Analytics team has prepared a dataset of 50 million transaction rows, which is stored in a partitioned BigQuery table. The team consists primarily of SQL experts with limited experience in Python or TensorFlow. You need to build a binary classification model to predict the likelihood of a customer making a purchase in the next seven days. You need to provide daily batch predictions. You need to minimize development effort, data movement, and the overall complexity of the solution. What should you do?

options.A: Create a model with BigQuery ML that includes the MODEL_TYPE=AUTOML_CLASSIFIER settings. Use the ML.PREDICT function to generate predictions as part of your nightly data warehouse jobs.
options.B: Use the BigQuery ML TRANSFORM function to normalize and scale numerical features, one-hot encode categorical features, and train a MODEL_TYPE=LOGISTIC_REG mode. Use the ML.PREDICT function to generate predictions as part of your nightly data warehouse jobs.
options.C: Train a classification model with Agent Platform AutoML Tabular Workflows, deploy the trained model to an Agent Platform endpoint, and add a nightly Cloud Run job to trigger batch predictions.
options.D: Develop an XGBoost model on an Agent Platform Workbench notebook. Load the data into a pandas DataFrame, and pickle it to a Cloud Storage bucket. Create another notebook that loads the pickled model from Cloud Storage and saves predictions back to Cloud Storage. Schedule this notebook for nightly execution.

discussion: Selected Answer: A Correct answer: A. BigQuery ML AutoML classification lets the SQL-focused team train a binary classifier directly on the partitioned BigQuery data and use ML.PREDICT for daily batch predictions, minimizing development effort and data movement; B requires manually designing preprocessing and a specific model, C adds Agent Platform deployment and Cloud Run infrastructure, and D requires substantial Python, data movement, and notebook management. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: BigQuery ML (BQML) with `AUTOML_CLASSIFIER` satisfies all requirements by keeping data directly within BigQuery (zero data movement), allowing the SQL-centric team to build and query models using familiar SQL syntax, and automatically handling feature engineering and model selection with minimal development effort. Option B requires manual feature transformations and limits model complexity to logistic regression, while Options C and D introduce unnecessary data movement, custom Python code, and operational complexity.

question: You have deployed a deep learning model to an Agent Platform endpoint using a machine type with NVIDIA GPUs. You initially configured the endpoint to autoscale based on a target CPU utilization of 60%. During a load test, you observe that prediction latency increases significantly as traffic rises, but the number of replicas remains constant. Cloud Monitoring indicates that CPU utilization stays below 40%, while the GPU utilization consistently exceeds 90%. You need to ensure that the endpoint scales efficiently to handle the increased load. What should you do?

options.A: Update the autoscaling configuration to scale based on the GPU duty cycle metric.
options.B: Update the autoscaling configuration to decrease the target CPU utilization to 20%.
options.C: Redeploy the model to a machine type that includes a TPU.
options.D: Increase the minimum replica count for the endpoint to match the peak load that was observed during testing.

discussion: Selected Answer: A Correct answer: A. Because the GPU is the actual bottleneck while CPU utilization remains low, configuring autoscaling based on the GPU duty cycle allows replicas to scale when GPU demand increases; B would not trigger scaling because CPU is already below the threshold, C unnecessarily changes accelerator types, and D wastes resources by permanently provisioning replicas for peak demand instead of autoscaling. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: The endpoint is currently bottlenecked by GPU utilization, which exceeds 90% while CPU utilization remains below the 60% threshold, preventing the autoscaler from adding replicas. Updating the autoscaling configuration to use the GPU duty cycle metric ensures that replica scaling is triggered directly by GPU load, effectively resolving latency issues during high traffic. Adjusting CPU targets or min replicas fails to address the root metric mismatch, and migrating to TPUs is unnecessary.

• D: Pinning min_replica_count to peak load disables cost-effective elasticity and wastes expensive GPU node hours during low-traffic periods.

question: Your company manages an ecommerce platform and has a large dataset of customer reviews. Each review has a positive, negative, or neutral label. options.B: Use Agent Platform AutoML to train a multi-class classification model that predicts sentiment labels based on the training data.
options.C: Use the Natural Language API for real-time sentiment analysis.
options.D: Train a sentiment analysis model by using a BERT-based model, and fine-tune the model by using domain-specific customer reviews.

gemini_rationale: Using AutoML for multi-class text classification allows you to leverage your existing labeled dataset to build a custom, accurate sentiment analysis model with minimal effort, code, and training time. question: You have a high-traffic ecommerce application that uses a recommendation model deployed on an Agent Platform endpoint. During flash sales, traffic quickly spikes from 1,000 to 50,000 queries per second (QPS). During these spikes, the application returns 503: Service Unavailable errors because the autoscaler cannot provision new resources quickly enough to meet the sudden demand. Your need to eliminate service disruptions during the start of the sale. How should you configure the endpoint?

options.A: Change the machine type to an a2-highgpu-1g instance with an NVIDIA A100 GPU.
options.B: Increase the min_replica_count to a baseline that covers a significant portion of the expected spike, and set the max_replica_count to 100.

options.D: Deploy the model to a private Agent Platform endpoint, and autoscale based on GPU utilization.

question: You lead an ML team at a financial technology company. Your team is building a system to detect potentially fraudulent credit card transactions in real-time. The model must return a prediction with very low latency (under 200ms) to approve or deny the transaction. The system must also scale to handle millions of transactions per day. Your dataset consists of structured, tabular transaction data stored in BigQuery. Your team is proficient in data science but wants to avoid the complexity of managing and optimizing a real-time model serving infrastructure. What should you do?

options.A: In an Agent Platform Workbench notebook, build a deep neural network (DNN) using PyTorch. Provision a cluster of GPU-enabled Compute Engine instances, and create an API to serve the model for real-time predictions.
options.B: Use BigQuery ML to train a boosted tree classification model. Schedule a batch prediction job using the ML.PREDICT function that runs every minute and scores recent transactions.
options.C: Use Forecasting with Agent Platform AutoML to train a time-series model on the sequence of transactions. Deploy the model as a tabular workflow to predict which future time windows are likely to contain fraudulent activity.
options.D: Use Agent Platform AutoML to train using your tabular dataset from BigQuery. Deploy the trained model to an Agent Platform endpoint, and integrate the endpoint’s API into your transaction processing application.

discussion: Selected Answer: D Correct answer: D. Agent Platform AutoML can train directly on tabular data from BigQuery and deploy the model to a managed endpoint that automatically handles scalable real-time serving with low latency; A requires substantial infrastructure management, B uses batch prediction and cannot reliably meet a sub-200 ms per-transaction requirement, and C is inappropriate because fraud detection is a classification problem rather than time-series forecasting. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Vertex AI (referred to here as Agent Platform) AutoML allows training models directly from tabular data in BigQuery without managing custom code or infrastructure. Deploying the model to a managed Vertex AI Endpoint provides scalable, low-latency real-time online predictions (under 200ms) required for real-time transaction processing. Option A requires significant infrastructure management, Option B is a batch-oriented approach that cannot achieve real-time transaction approvals, and Option C uses time-series forecasting instead of per-transaction classification.

question: You are training a ResNet-50 computer vision model on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform using a custom PyTorch container. The training job is configured with a generic machine type and one NVIDIA A100 GPU. During the training, you monitor the resource utilization charts. You observe that the GPU utilization is volatile, frequently dropping to 0% for short intervals, while the CPU utilization remains consistently above 90%. You want to maximize GPU utilization to reduce training time. What should you do?

options.A: Increase the training batch size to saturate the GPU memory.
options.B: Update the DataLoader utility to increase the num_workers parameter and enable pin_memory.
options.C: Switch to a machine type with a higher number of GPUs, and implement the torch.nn.parallel.DistributedDataParallel strategy in the training code.
options.D: Enable automatic mixed precision (AMP) to speed up the matrix multiplications.

discussion: Selected Answer: B Correct answer: B. The high CPU usage and intermittent 0% GPU utilization indicate the GPU is waiting for data, so increasing DataLoader workers and enabling pin_memory improves data-loading throughput and keeps the GPU fed; A may increase memory pressure without fixing the CPU bottleneck, C adds GPUs without addressing the data pipeline bottleneck, and D can speed up GPU computation but does not resolve the CPU-side data-loading starvation. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: High CPU utilization combined with GPU utilization dropping to 0% indicates a data loading and preprocessing bottleneck where the GPU is starving for data. Increasing `num_workers` in PyTorch's `DataLoader` allows asynchronous parallel data loading on the CPU, and setting `pin_memory=True` enables faster copy operations from CPU to GPU memory. Options A, C, and D focus on GPU computation speed or capacity, which will not resolve the CPU-bound data pipeline bottleneck.

❌ Why Others Fail:
• A: Increasing batch size increases GPU memory usage without accelerating per-image CPU decoding or host-to-device data prefetching.
• C: Adding more GPUs with DistributedDataParallel accelerates device compute while exacerbating the existing CPU data-pipeline bottleneck.
• D: Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP) speeds up A100 Tensor Core math on the GPU, causing the GPU to finish batches even faster and wait longer at 0% on the CPU DataLoader.

question: You are building an ML workflow that preprocesses data, trains a model with hyperparameter tuning, and deploys the best model to an Agent Platform endpoint. Your preprocessing step takes two hours and outputs a 100 GB dataset. You run experiments daily with different model architectures using the same preprocessing step. You need to automate this process and optimize the pipeline runs to minimize cost and time. What should you do?

options.A: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow with a single component for the preprocessing and training steps. Use Agent Platform hyperparameter tuning jobs within the component to identify optimal parameters.
options.B: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow with separate components for the preprocessing and training steps. Enable caching on the preprocessing component, and use Agent Platform Serverless Training custom jobs for the training steps.
options.C: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow with separate components for the preprocessing and training steps. Use a Cloud Run function to trigger the pipeline, and configure Agent Platform Serverless Training custom jobs for the training steps.
options.D: Configure an Agent Platform Pipelines workflow that starts with an Agent Platform Serverless Training custom job for the preprocessing step. Use a Cloud Run function to launch the hyperparameter tuning job that is triggered when the preprocessed data arrives in Cloud Storage.

discussion: Selected Answer: B Correct answer: B. Separating preprocessing and training enables caching of the expensive two-hour, 100 GB preprocessing step so it can be reused across experiments, while Serverless Training efficiently handles the model training jobs; A prevents effective reuse by combining the steps, C adds an unnecessary Cloud Run trigger without addressing preprocessing reuse, and D adds unnecessary orchestration and storage-trigger complexity. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Separating the preprocessing and training steps into distinct pipeline components allows you to enable execution caching on the preprocessing component. Since the preprocessing step is identical for daily experiments, caching avoids re-running the expensive 2-hour job and reusing the output dataset, significantly saving time and costs.

question: You are an ML engineer at a retail company. You need to automate a recurring retraining workflow for a demand forecasting model. The workflow involves dependencies across hybrid environments and must execute the following sequential steps: 1. Trigger a shell script on an on-premises server to extract legacy sales data and send it to a Cloud Storage bucket. 2. Trigger a pipeline in Agent Platform Pipelines to train and validate the new model. 3. Push the validation metrics to a third-party API. You need a fully managed orchestration service that provides native connectors to handle these cross-platform dependencies. You want to use the most stable, robust solution. What should you do?

options.A: Use Workflows to define the orchestration logic in YAML. Use the http.post connector to trigger the on-premises shell script and the Agent Platform API for the training job.
options.B: Use Cloud Scheduler to trigger a Cloud Run function that executes the on-premises script using SSH, publishes a Pub/Sub message upon completion, and triggers the subsequent workflow steps.
options.C: Use Managed Service for Apache Airflow to define a directed acyclic graph (DAG) in Python. Use Apache Airflow operators and sensors to orchestrate the workflow steps.
options.D: Use Agent Platform Pipelines to develop a custom container component for each workflow step. Use the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK to define the execution order.

Managed Service for Apache Airflow is a fully managed orchestration platform built for complex workflows with cross-environment dependencies, and its operators/sensors provide robust integration with external systems; A relies on Workflows connectors that may not directly support executing an on-premises shell script, B requires custom SSH/Pub/Sub infrastructure, and D unnecessarily uses ML pipeline components for broader infrastructure orchestration. upvoted 1 times

question: You are developing an automated training workflow using Agent Platform Pipelines. The pipeline trains a new custom model and registers it to Model Registry. You need to validate the model’s performance on a held-out test dataset. You want to ensure that the model is deployed to a production Agent Platform endpoint only if its evaluation metrics meet a specific threshold. You want to minimize cost and administrative overhead. What should you do?

options.A: Configure the training component to calculate evaluation metrics on the training dataset during the training job. Output the metrics to the next step and use a conditional task to deploy the model if the evaluation metrics exceed the specified threshold.
options.B: Insert a Python component that pulls the latest model version from Model Registry. Compare its training metrics against the current production model, and use a conditional task to deploy the new model if it performs better.
options.C: Deploy the model to a temporary Agent Platform endpoint. Use a custom component to send the test dataset for online prediction, calculate the metrics, and deploy to the production endpoint if the evaluation metrics exceed the specified threshold.
options.D: Add a batch prediction component to generate predictions on the test dataset. Pass the results to a model evaluation component. Use a conditional task to deploy the model if the evaluation metrics exceed the specified threshold.

discussion: Selected Answer: D Correct answer: D. A batch prediction step can efficiently generate predictions on the held-out test set, and a model evaluation component can calculate the required metrics before a conditional deployment, avoiding the cost of deploying a temporary endpoint; A evaluates on the training data instead of the held-out set, B compares training metrics rather than test performance, and C incurs unnecessary online endpoint deployment and inference costs. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Using a batch prediction component to generate predictions on a held-out test dataset followed by a model evaluation component is the standard, cost-effective way to evaluate models in Vertex AI Pipelines. It avoids the compute overhead and cost of deploying to a temporary online endpoint (Option C) and correctly evaluates on a test dataset rather than training metrics (Options A and B).

question: You are developing a machine learning pipeline using the Kubeflow Pipelines (KFP) SDK that will run on Agent Platform Pipelines. The pipeline includes a preprocessing component that takes two hours to transform a large dataset. You are currently iterating on the code for the subsequent model_training component and need to re-submit the pipeline frequently for testing. You need to ensure that the preprocessing component only re-runs if its inputs or parameters have changed. You want to minimize effort, costs, and total execution time. What should you do?

options.A: Ensure that execution caching is enabled for the preprocessing component by including the set_caching_options(enable_caching=True) method.
options.B: Track the run lineage using Agent Platform Experiments, and pass the output artifact URI from the previous run into the training component.
options.C: Configure the pipeline to write the preprocessed data to a persistent volume claim (PVC) that is shared across pipeline runs.
options.D: Add a dsl.Condition step to the pipeline that checks if the preprocessing step has executed in the last hour.

discussion: Selected Answer: A Correct answer: A. KFP execution caching automatically reuses the preprocessing result when its inputs and parameters are unchanged, avoiding the two-hour recomputation and reducing cost and runtime; B requires manual artifact management, C adds unnecessary persistent-storage complexity, and D uses a time-based condition instead of KFP’s built-in input/parameter-based caching. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Execution caching in Kubeflow Pipelines and Vertex AI Pipelines automatically skips execution and reuses the output artifacts of a task if its code, parameters, and inputs have not changed from a previous run. Using `set_caching_options(enable_caching=True)` minimizes effort and execution cost without requiring custom conditional logic or manual artifact tracking.

question: You are an ML engineer at a large retail company. You have a BigQuery table containing five years of daily sales data for 50,000 distinct product SKUs. You need to generate a daily demand forecast for the next 30 days for each individual SKU. The solution must automatically account for holidays and weekly seasonality. You want to minimize data egress costs and operational complexity by keeping the data and model within the data warehouse. What should you do?

options.A: Use the CREATE MODEL... OPTIONS(model_type='ARIMA_PLUS') statement in BigQuery to generate a forecast based on historical SKU sales.
options.B: Use the gcloud ai custom-jobs create command to run a PyTorch LSTM container on Agent Platform that pulls data from a CSV into Cloud Storage.
options.C: Use the CREATE MODEL... OPTIONS(model_type='LINEAR_REG') statement in BigQuery to predict sales using the transaction date as a feature.
options.D: Use the google-cloud-aiplatform SDK to create a TimeSeriesDataset and trigger an AutoMLForecastingTrainingJob.

discussion: Selected Answer: A Correct answer: A. BigQuery ML’s ARIMA_PLUS is designed for time-series forecasting directly within BigQuery and can automatically model seasonality and holiday effects while keeping the data and model in the warehouse; B and D move the workload to Agent Platform, adding operational complexity and potential data movement, while C’s linear regression does not natively handle time-series seasonality and holiday effects. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: BigQuery ML's ARIMA_PLUS model is built specifically for time-series forecasting, automatically handling holiday effects, trend, and weekly/yearly seasonality directly inside BigQuery. This eliminates data egress costs and minimizes operational complexity by keeping the entire ML pipeline within the data warehouse, while natively supporting multiple time-series across 50,000 SKUs via the TIME_SERIES_ID_COL option.

question: Your team is deploying a real-time personalized ad-ranking model. The model requires low-latency access for hundreds of user-level features to be fetched at request time. options.B: Enable Agent Platform Feature Store, and use the FetchFeatureValues API to fetch features for the model.
options.C: Implement a Redis cache on Memorystore, and add a component to the Dataflow pipeline to write the feature to the Redis cache.
options.D: Use BigQuery BI Engine to accelerate the SQL queries used to fetch features.

discussion: Selected Answer: B Correct answer: B. gemini_rationale: Vertex AI Feature Store (or Agent Platform Feature Store) is a fully managed service designed specifically for ultra-low latency online feature serving and point lookups at scale with minimal operational overhead. Options A and D do not provide the millisecond point-lookup latencies required for online ML inference at request time. Option C introduces significant operational overhead for managing custom Dataflow pipeline sync components and Redis infrastructure.

question: You are optimizing the training of a 175-billion parameter LLM on Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform. You have provisioned a TPU v5p Pod slice with 32 chips for the job. You initially ran the training using standard data parallelism, but the job immediately failed with an out-of-memory (OOM) error. You need to implement a training strategy that resolves the memory issue and minimizes training latency. What should you do?

options.A: Configure the training to use a parameter server architecture where the model weights are stored in the host CPU memory.
options.B: Enable gradient checkpointing, and continue using the data parallelism strategy.
options.C: Configure the training to shard the model parameters and optimizer states, and continue using the data parallelism strategy.
options.D: Scale up the TPU Pod slice to include more chips, and continue using the data parallelism strategy.

discussion: Selected Answer: C Correct answer: C. Sharding the model parameters and optimizer states across the TPU chips reduces the per-chip memory footprint while preserving data parallelism, resolving the OOM issue efficiently; A introduces CPU-memory and communication bottlenecks, B mainly reduces activation memory and does not sufficiently address the huge parameter/optimizer memory footprint, and D adds more hardware and cost rather than using memory-efficient sharding. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: A 175-billion parameter model requires over 2 TB of memory per device to store model weights, gradients, and optimizer states, which vastly exceeds the memory capacity of a single TPU v5p chip (95 GB). Sharding the model parameters and optimizer states across the TPU chips (such as with Fully Sharded Data Parallelism/ZeRO-3) distributes this memory footprint across the cluster to resolve OOM errors while preserving high throughput. Options B and D fail because standard data parallelism requires every chip to replicate the entire model state, which cannot fit on a single chip regardless of gradient checkpointing or adding more chips.

notebook_source_ref: Source #1 (PMLE June 2026 Exam Guide §3.3) & Source #5 (Google Cloud TPU v5p Architecture & FSDP/GSPMD Sharding Docs)
notebook_rationale:
✅ Why C is Correct: A 175B-parameter LLM requires ~2.8 TB for weights, gradients, and Adam optimizer states, exceeding a single TPU v5p chip's 95 GiB HBM under pure data parallelism; sharding parameters and optimizer states across all 32 chips (~3.04 TiB aggregate HBM via FSDP/GSPMD over high-speed ICI) eliminates per-chip OOM while preserving data-parallel throughput and low latency.
❌ Why Others Fail:
• A: Offloading weights to host CPU parameter servers bottlenecks every step on slow host-device transfers and ignores TPU Inter-Chip Interconnect (ICI) collective sharding.
• B: Gradient checkpointing only reduces activation memory; replicating ~2.8 TB of unsharded parameters and optimizer states on each 95 GiB chip still immediately OOMs.
• D: Adding more TPU chips under unsharded data parallelism still replicates the full 175B model state onto every individual 95 GiB chip, failing with the exact same OOM error.

question: You have deployed a custom classification model to an Agent Platform endpoint to predict the likelihood of customer churn in real-time. You need to collect the data to calculate the model’s exact precision and recall by comparing production predictions with ground truth data in BigQuery. You want to minimize development effort. What should you do?

options.A: Modify the prediction container to asynchronously write the prediction result to BigQuery after every request.
options.B: Schedule a daily Agent Platform batch prediction job that uses the same model resource as the deployed endpoint and stores predictions in BigQuery.
options.C: Update the model deployment parameters to enable request-response logging to BigQuery. Set the sampling rate to 1.0.
options.D: Create a model evaluation job by providing the model resource and the BigQuery ground truth table to calculate precision and recall.

discussion: Selected Answer: C Correct answer: C. Enabling request-response logging with a 1.0 sampling rate captures every production request and prediction in BigQuery, providing the prediction data needed to join with ground truth and calculate exact precision and recall with minimal development effort; A adds custom application code, B creates unnecessary batch predictions instead of capturing real-time traffic, and D cannot calculate production precision/recall unless the production predictions have first been collected. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Enabling request-response logging to BigQuery with a sampling rate of 1.0 is a managed Vertex AI feature that captures 100% of real-time endpoint predictions directly into BigQuery with zero code changes, minimizing development effort. question: You are in the exploratory phase of development of a demand forecasting model. Several terabytes of historical sales and inventory records are stored in a BigQuery table. You need to create a new, clean table to perform preliminary analyses on metrics, such as moving averages of sales figures and weekly aggregates, without additional data movement. You want to use the simplest approach and minimize overhead. What should you do?

options.A: Create a PreprocessingOp component in the Agent Platform Pipelines workflow to compute the moving averages and extract time-based features and write the processed data to a new destination table in BigQuery.
options.B: Read the data from BigQuery into a Dask DataFrame using Agent Platform Workbench. Perform exploratory data analysis (EDA) and feature engineering transformations, and write the processed data back to a new destination table in BigQuery.
options.C: Write a SQL query in the BigQuery console. Use the ML.TRANSFORM function in BigQuery ML to compute the moving averages and extract time-based features. Write the processed data to a new destination table in BigQuery.
options.D: Write a SQL query in the BigQuery console. Use standard SQL functions like CAST, EXTRACT, and window functions with OVER() clauses to perform the transformations and calculations. Materialize the results into a new destination table in BigQuery.

discussion: Selected Answer: D Correct answer: D. BigQuery SQL can perform the required aggregations, window functions, and feature transformations directly where the data resides, avoiding data movement and minimizing development and infrastructure overhead. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: Using standard BigQuery SQL functions (such as window functions and date/time functions) to query and materialize the results directly into a new BigQuery table requires zero data movement, utilizes BigQuery's scalable compute engine, and minimizes operational overhead. Options A and B introduce unnecessary architecture overhead and data movement, while ML.TRANSFORM in Option C is designed specifically for preprocessing within BigQuery ML model definitions rather than general SQL table materialization.

question: You work for a healthcare organization and need to automate the patient triage process. question: You work for an international bank. Your team is developing a generative AI application that summarizes complex financial reports. You need to implement an automated, scalable solution to evaluate and quantify the quality of generated summaries against the previous version of the solution. What should you do?

options.A: Use Model Monitoring to track the prediction drift of the token output length.
options.B: Run an automatic side-by-side (AutoSxS) evaluation job in Agent Platform to compare outputs from the new and previous versions of the solution.
options.C: Deploy both versions of the solution, and use A/B testing to route a portion of production traffic to the new version and route the remaining traffic to the previous version. Compare user click-through rates.
options.D: Run an evaluation job in Agent Platform, and calculate a BLEU score to compare the new and previous versions of the solution.

discussion: Selected Answer: B Correct answer: B. AutoSxS evaluation automatically compares outputs from the new and previous versions using scalable, model-based quality metrics, making it well suited for objectively evaluating generative AI summaries without relying on production traffic. upvoted 1 times
gemini_rationale: AutoSxS (Automatic Side-by-Side) evaluation uses an LLM-as-a-judge to perform automated, scalable, and nuanced comparisons between outputs of two generative AI models, making it ideal for evaluating summary quality against a baseline. BLEU scores rely on strict n-gram overlaps which perform poorly for flexible generative summaries, while tracking token length or click-through rates fails to quantify actual summary content quality.

question: You are deploying a generative AI chatbot for an online gaming community using Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform.
